# Revised sampling review of the saved 500 year populations

The previous control sampling passed. The compensatory population passed its other 27 required checks, but its exact local allocation failed. This review changes sampling allocation only. It preserves the ecological histories and the earlier sampling failure.

Reuse each history's original 480 captured adults, with 30 in each of sixteen 75 m strata. Retain exactly 160 adults aged at least five years, with exactly 40 in each 150 m quadrant. Allow 5 to 15 retained animals per smaller stratum. Favor the allocation closest to ten per stratum before applying the fixed seed-90401 priority among feasible solutions. The quadrant totals preserve broad coverage; the smaller-stratum bounds prevent the selected sample from concentrating within a quadrant.

Keep at least 10 m between every pair and retain no more than one animal per 10 m cell. Exclude pairs sharing any recorded parent or grandparent, and exclude direct parent or grandparent relationships. Require complete two-generation records for every candidate. More distant relatives can remain, so this design does not claim complete genealogical independence.

Use one optimization attempt per history, one computational thread, a 60 second solver limit and the original seed. No replacement capture pool, alternative seed, fallback allocation rule, genetic response, movement outcome, reproductive contribution or environmental value may influence selection. If the revised design fails, preserve that result rather than changing it within this review.

Independently audit every retained ID against the original capture and year-500 checkpoint. Rebuild its two-generation ancestry from the birth ledger, and check all 12,720 retained pairs using scalar distances and cell coordinates. Check every geographic allocation, age, coordinate and pedigree record. Report minimum and median nearest-neighbor distance, counts by stratum and quadrant, distinct cells, and all excluded relationship violations. These checks establish sampling feasibility; they do not establish genetic IBR recovery or full demographic equilibrium.
